thesis: Abstract domains make selected properties available through sound approximation, with precision and cost traded explicitly.
role: Ground interpretive plurality in established verification methods.

ideas.statement: Abstract domains make selected properties available through sound approximation, with precision and cost traded explicitly.
ideas.recurrenceCandidate: Ground interpretive plurality in established verification methods.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Independent intervals lose x=y and return a broad difference while a relational domain proves zero.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Empirical success does not prove abstract soundness; fixed-point iteration needs stopping mechanisms and incomplete verification remains qualified.

audit.notes: Source-grounded analysis; proposed mechanisms and limited guarantees preserved.
